subject: Onboarding readiness & environment playbook — HealthCore POC
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@healthcore.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Onboarding readiness & environment playbook — HealthCore POC

Hi Emma —

Good to see the go-ahead this morning. Per our call, I put together a concise readiness playbook so we can keep the POC kickoff on track and unblocked for the May evaluation window. Attached is a working MAP spreadsheet (healthcore-map-v1.xlsx) and a simple peering diagram.

Top-line asks for POC environment (minimal required items):
- Org & initial admin user created in Redwood Console (requested owner: HealthCore IT)
- API key for evaluation (scoped to test environment; rotate after canary)
- IP allowlist for initial workers: HealthCore will provide CIDR ranges for allowlist; Redwood needs these for control-plane egress and peering verification
- VPC peering request + routing acceptance (customer-owned VPC)
- Signed SOW or acknowledgement of trial terms (DocuSign link to follow)

Proposed deadlines (mutual action items):
1) By 2027-05-03: Redwood to provision trial org, create first API key, and share secure access instructions (owner: marissa_cole).
2) By 2027-05-05: HealthCore to provide IP ranges and submit VPC peering request (owner: Emma Li / security@healthcore.com).
3) By 2027-05-07: Exchange test credentials and perform a canary run for 100 requests (owner: evelyn_hart).
4) By 2027-05-10: Finalize SOW acceptance for production-readiness discussion (owner: HealthCore procurement / sergio_alvarez).

Questions / clarifications we need from your side to avoid delays:
- Preferred method for receiving the initial API key (secure vault link vs. direct in-console creation)?
- Any egress firewall rules beyond IP allowlist we should expect?
- Will you need us to open a support ticket with your cloud vendor for peering, or do you own that step?

Next steps: I’ll loop in the network engineer on our side (Evelyn) to coordinate CIDR validation once you send the ranges. Marissa will draft the org and seed the test key as soon as we have the peer request.

Thanks — looking forward to a smooth kickoff.

—
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: healthcore-map-v1.xlsx, network-peering-diagram.png
From: Emma Li <emma.li@healthcore.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: CISO Procurement <security@healthcore.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding readiness & environment playbook — HealthCore POC

Thanks, Sergio — this is helpful. A couple quick notes from my side:

- We prefer the API key via our Secrets Manager; could you provide steps for secure ingestion?
- Our security team (copied) will own CIDR ranges and peering approvals — they may ask for a short meeting to confirm routing policies.
- One constraint: our infra team will only accept peering requests from the 3rd–7th May window due to a maintenance freeze the week of May 2. Is that workable?

Also, can you confirm whether Redwood needs to initiate the peering, or if we should submit the request from our cloud console? We typically have to create the request and then the peer accepts.

Emma
VP Product, HealthCore
emma.li@healthcore.com | +1 617-555-6677
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@healthcore.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Markus Johansson <m.johnson@cloudops.io>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 13:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding readiness & environment playbook — HealthCore POC

Hi Emma — thanks for the note and for looping in security.

Short answers up front:
- We will provide a short Secrets Manager ingest play (steps + CLI snippet) and can deliver via Drive link or paste into your secure vault ticket.
- For peering: typically the customer originates the peer request (your cloud console), and Redwood accepts. That fits your maintenance freeze window — if you kick the request between May 3–5 we’ll accept and validate routing that week.

Updated mutual action plan with owners and firm dates (we’ll keep this in the MAP spreadsheet):
- Action A — Create HealthCore Redwood org and initial admin user (owner: HealthCore / Emma Li) — target: 2027-05-01 (soft), 2027-05-03 (hard).
- Action B — Redwood creates evaluation API key scoped to test org, posts secure ingest instructions (owner: marissa_cole@redwood.com) — target: 2027-05-03.
- Action C — HealthCore opens VPC peering request + provides CIDRs and egress rules (owner: security@healthcore.com) — open window: 2027-05-03 to 2027-05-05.
- Action D — Redwood validates peering, updates route tables, and runs network handshake (owner: evelyn_hart@redwood.com) — target: 2027-05-06.
- Action E — Canary run (100 requests) and initial quality checks (owner: evelyn_hart / HealthCore dev) — target: 2027-05-07.
- Action F — Close readiness checkpoint and finalize SOW for follow-on (owner: sergio_alvarez / HealthCore procurement) — target: 2027-05-10.

Security details for your engineers (Evelyn copied):
- Required allowlist: control-plane egress to 34.120.200.0/24 and 34.120.201.0/24 for the initial test fleet.
- Peering: we support standard peering with route propagation disabled; we will provide the peer VPC ID after org creation.
- API keys: we recommend generating in-console and exporting to your Secrets Manager via the CLI snippet we will share. Keys are revocable and scoped to the trial org.

Attachments referenced: sow-healthcore-draft.pdf (for SOW language), network-peering-diagram.png

I’ll put the final MAP into HubSpot and share the link to the DocuSign SOW once we have the org confirmed.

—
Sergio

On a related note, Markus (cc) from CloudOps suggested he can help expedite the peering validation if you want an external reviewer on the cloud side. Markus — any quick guidance on common gotchas?
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Emma Li <emma.li@healthcore.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding readiness & environment playbook — HealthCore POC

Thanks — I’ll take Action B. Plan:
- Create trial org and an admin user today (2027-04-30).
- Create scoped API key and export to a secure vault entry; I will send an ingestion snippet for HashiCorp Vault and AWS Secrets Manager.
- Post the secure vault link to the HubSpot MAP and email only the HealthCore admin user (per Emma’s preference).

Timeline note: I will have the key uploaded and instructions to you by 2027-05-03 EOD PT. If you need the key earlier for any automation, tell me and I can accelerate.

—
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachment: sow-healthcore-draft.pdf
From: Emma Li <emma.li@healthcore.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: CISO Procurement <security@healthcore.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding readiness & environment playbook — HealthCore POC

Appreciate the clarity, team. We’ll aim to open the peering request on 2027-05-03 and provide CIDRs that morning. Security has asked for a 48-hour buffer after the handshake to run policy checks — does Redwood need that window before the canary? If so, we’ll shift the canary to 2027-05-09 to accommodate.

We’re comfortable with the secure-vault approach for the API key — please only send the link to the admin user once the org is created. Also confirm when you post the MAP in HubSpot so procurement can reference it in the SOW review.

If everyone is aligned, consider this confirmation of the schedule with a small ask to move the canary to 2027-05-09 to give our infra team breathing room.

Emma
VP Product, HealthCore
